comments.text:
The following code:

```
s <- socketConnection(port = 8083L, open = "")
socketSelect(list(s), timeout = 0)
```

Resulted in this output:

```
 *** caught segfault ***
address 0x7e69dddd8df8, cause 'memory not mapped'

Traceback:
 1: socketSelect(list(s), timeout = 0)
An irrecoverable exception occurred. R is aborting now ...
Segmentation fault (core dumped)
```

To reproduce: 
```
Rscript -e 's <- socketConnection(port = 8083L, open = ""); socketSelect(list(s), timeout = 0)'
```

comments.creator: kevinushey
comments.text:
Created attachment 4041
socketSelect(): reject unopened socket connections, initialize sockconn fields

This is an uninitialized read, so the result depends on what malloc() returns. in_R_newsock() leaves fd, pstart and pend for sock_open() to set, and do_sockselect() uses them without checking that the connection is open.

On macOS the struct comes back zeroed, so fd is 0 and the call quietly select()s on stdin; that is the FALSE in comment 1. On Linux a negative value gives the reported segfault (an abort on fortified builds such as Ubuntu's), which I can force with

    GLIBC_TUNABLES=glibc.malloc.perturb=85 Rscript -e 's <- socketConnection(port = 8083L, open = ""); socketSelect(list(s), timeout = 0)'

The attached patch makes socketSelect() signal "connection is not open" for such a connection, initializes the three fields and adds a regression test. Patch also at https://github.com/r-devel/r-svn/pull/475
